fields.description: The engine/discipline this retirement belongs to (e.g. 'Electrical'). The read function returns the two lists scoped to one discipline, which is the shape the asset uses.
fields.label: Discipline

fields.description: Which axis this retirement is on: 'kind' retires a master-item kind (loader retired_kinds), 'category' retires a category config (loader retired_category_ids). The two axes are NOT symmetric -- switches_point owned no item kinds at all (a pure borrower of switch_socket_item), so its retirement has a config footprint and no item footprint.
fields.label: Scope Type

fields.description: The retired kind name (e.g. 'ups_per_kva') or category_id (e.g. 'switches_point').
fields.label: Scope Value

fields.description: When this was retired. OPTIONAL, and DELIBERATELY EMPTY on the backfilled rows: the loader never recorded when, and the only available signal is a batch creation timestamp, which is approximate. A field asserting a precision it does not have is worse than an empty one -- do NOT back-infer it.
fields.label: Retired At

fields.description: Who retired it. OPTIONAL, and DELIBERATELY EMPTY on the backfilled rows for the same reason as retired_at -- the loader never recorded it and it must not be invented.
fields.label: Retired By

fields.description: Why it was retired, in the owner's words. OPTIONAL and empty on the backfill. The asset's excluded_categories prose carried reasons for some of these, but that key is archaeology the export deliberately drops, so it is not migrated here.
fields.label: Reason
